rationale:
The `{cite}` of `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` on `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageLog]` is the right role.

- **Not a test.** `UsageLog` is a plain struct.
- **Not an `{impl}` root.** The requirement is already implemented by marked items that reach `UsageLog`. These are `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_output]`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]`, `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[persisted]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[PendingAssessment]/fn[failed]`. `UsageLog` is reached by following those items through the types they use, so it needs no `{impl}`. The serialized record fields are declared in `UsageRecord`, not in `UsageLog`. `UsageLog` only wraps the record with its file `path`, timers and a callback.
- **`{cite}` fits.** `UsageLog.path` is the location of the per-run JSON record at `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`. `UsageLog.record` is the usage record that gets persisted. A change to the requirement's per-run file location or its record persistence could require changing this struct. The item relies on that behaviour without implementing or testing it.
- **No redundancy.** The struct has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement.

text: Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
